title: Exact log-depth preparation of highly entangled matrix product states
authors: Keisuke Murota, Frédéric Sauvage, Marco Ballarin, Gabriel Matos, Enrico Rinaldi
abstract: Preparing matrix product states (MPS) on a quantum device is a key subroutine in many quantum algorithms. The most competitive methods, based on the renormalisation group, prepare translationally invariant MPS of size $L$ and bond dimension $χ$, up to an error $\varepsilon$, in circuit depth $\tilde O(χ^{4}\log(L/\varepsilon))$ or $\tilde O(χ^{6}\log\log(L/\varepsilon))$. We improve multiple aspects of these methods. First, using block-encoded correction maps, whose post-selection succeeds with constant probability, we render the preparation exact without sacrificing the scaling in $L$. Second, through a generalisation of oblivious amplitude amplification to isometries, we reduce the bond-dimension dependence, improving the depth to $\tilde O(χ^{2}\log L + χ^{4})$ or $\tilde O(χ^{2}\log\log L + χ^{4})$, and even to $\tilde O(χ^{3}\log L)$ for incoherent preparations. Finally, we extend the framework to non-translationally invariant MPS and prove logarithmic-depth exact preparation for independent and identically distributed random tensor sequences. Confirmed by numerical studies, these results constitute, to the best of our knowledge, the most efficient exact MPS preparation protocols in the relevant parameter regimes.
summary: This paper presents advanced theoretical protocols for preparing Matrix Product States (MPS) on a quantum computer. By integrating techniques like oblivious amplitude amplification and quasi-probabilistic decomposition, the authors achieve state-of-the-art scaling in circuit depth while ensuring exact preparation fidelity. This advances the practical feasibility of simulating complex quantum many-body systems.
main_problem: The central problem is developing quantum circuit protocols that can prepare highly entangled Matrix Product States (MPS) with high fidelity and minimal circuit depth.
main_result: The authors achieve state-of-the-art, exact preparation protocols for MPS, significantly improving the scaling of circuit depth dependence on both bond dimension ($\chi$) and system size ($L$).
method: They combine techniques like block-encoded correction maps, generalizations of oblivious amplitude amplification (OAAI), and quasi-probabilistic decomposition (QPD) to deterministically implement required isometries.
model_or_system: The focus is on preparing MPS states $|	ext{A}(L)angle$, which are efficient representations of quantum many-body ground states. The analysis involves tensor network manipulations, renormalization group flow concepts, and circuit depth scaling laws.
key_observables: Circuit depth (scaling with $\chi$ and $L$), success probability ($p_{	ext{succ}}$), residual norms ($\|R(q)\|$), and the required block size ($q$).
important_parameters: Bond dimension ($\chi$), System size ($L$), Error tolerance ($\epsilon$), Correlation length ($\xi$), and Block size parameters ($q, Q$).
main_assumptions: The analysis often relies on asymptotic scaling limits (e.g., large $L$ or small $\delta$) and the assumption that certain error terms decay exponentially with block size.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate circuit constructions for TI MPS preparation, comparing different protocols like All-at-Once vs. Split-and-Concatenate methods, and showing optimization landscapes for determining optimal block sizes ($Q \propto \sqrt{L'}$).
paper_structure: The paper systematically improves the protocol by first establishing approximate RG methods (Chunk 2), then introducing exact probabilistic corrections (Chunk 3), optimizing the implementation of isometries via amplitude amplification (Chunk 4), and finally refining the depth scaling using quasi-probabilistic techniques (Chunks 5, 6, 7, 8).
why_interesting: The work provides concrete, resource-aware quantum circuit blueprints for simulating complex many-body physics models that are computationally intractable classically.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Circuit construction for the preparation of a TI MPS with bond dimension χ (a). The representative circuit (b-d) sketched here corresponds to the method SeqAA of Ta- ble I. As detailed in Secs. II and III, the circuit consists of the preparation of an RG fixed point P (∞) (b), a layer of correc- tion maps C(q) (c), and a layer of isometries V (q) (d). Key to our circuit constructions are the correction maps (green rect- angles) implemented through block-encoding. These ensure exactness of the circuit preparations and are used to reduce the circuit depths for the isometries V (q).

FIG. 2. (a) The TI MPS to be prepared (2) after the steps of blocking (6) and polar decomposition (7). (b) For normal TI MPS, the tensor P (q) can be approximated through its fixed- point P (∞) (10) that can be prepared in O(χ2) depth (12). Together with the implementation of V (q) (20), this forms the basis of the efficient approximate MPS preparation of Malz et al. [39], with scalings reported in Table I. (c) Introducing a correction map C(q), implemented through block-encoding, one can achieve similar scalings for exact state preparation.

FIG. 3. Preparation of the renormalised state |P (q)(L′)⟩. a) All-at-once: all the correction maps C(q) are applied in par- allel. b) Split-and-concatenate: the corrections are first per- formed within splits (a subset of Q blocks, depicted here for Q = 4). When all splits have been corrected, a final round of correction maps between splits is performed to concatenate the L′/Q splits. Both prepare the same state. However, upon failure of one correction map, the whole procedure needs to be repeated for a) while only the preparation of the corre- sponding split is required for b).

FIG. 4. Ratio of estimated circuit depths between the SeqAA and RenAA implementations of V (q), shown as a function of the system size L (log scale) for bond dimensions χ ∈{2, 4, 8}. Each data point shows the mean ± one standard deviation over NMPS = 64 Haar-random TI MPS instances with cor- relation length ξ ≈3.3. Extrapolating from the data, the crossover at which RenAA becomes favourable for χ = 8 is estimated to occur at around L ∼1034.

FIG. 5. Estimated circuit depth as a function of the sys- tem size L (log scale) for the same ensemble of Haar-random TI MPS as in Fig. 4 for bond dimensions χ ∈{4, 8}. Each data point shows the mean ± one standard deviation over NMPS = 64 instances. We compare the approximate RG- based approach of Malz et al. [39] for trace-distance errors ε ∈{10−1, 10−2, 10−3} (grey) with our exact protocols: all- at-once (A@O) correction with sequential implementation of V (q) (blue), all-at-once (A@O) correction with SeqAA imple- mentation of V (q) (green), and split-and-concatenate (S&C) correction with sequential V (q) (orange).
